acceptance.text: Unified node creation exists from top-right plus and canvas right-click, offers Agent/File/Markdown/Diagram, and removes the old top-center Markdown/Diagram toolbar.

File/text ingestion works: Explorer drag creates workspace-reference File node; Explorer preview can insert File node; external drop/paste stores File node under Harness/user-files; large pasted text creates Markdown node.
Backend exposes a complete workspace file pipe: meta, byte read, bounded text read, HEAD, Range, MIME, traversal denial, stale/missing file state.
Agent-readable graph snapshot includes connected resource refs, handles, directions, stateRef, contentRef, and capability hints for File/Markdown/Diagram nodes.
Markdown default output is configurable per agent, target-selectable, and falls back to oldest connected Markdown when enabled with no explicit target.

Explorer interaction is deterministic: single-click folder toggles open/closed, file click opens preview, right-click menu uses global viewport coordinates and clamps in view, Explorer gestures do not pan/drag canvas.
Node interaction is deterministic: double-click opens config/editor; right-click opens node menu only; delete/settings/open config/copy/cut/duplicate actions are available with stable selectors.
Bridge edge interaction is stable: single-click/drag does not open panel, double-click opens panel, edge/offset persistence happens on commit only and survives reload without disconnections.
Markdown and Excalidraw editors have enlarged/fullscreen mode, smooth loading/open animation, real editor loaded state, save revisions, Excalidraw icon/brand styling, no useless Rect toolbar button.

Agent settings panel is searchable, categorized, compact, i18n-ready, has tooltips, selectors/switches for common config, explorer-backed cwd picker, working Add Skill, and no raw JSON for common permission/launch policy.
Overlay stack is deterministic: toasts render above workflow chrome, menus/panels clamp to viewport, fullscreen is top layer.

Performance budget holds on /workflow: no React update loop, no failed API resources, ready under 3s in seeded graph smoke, no long task above 250ms during key interactions, edge drag sends no graph-map PUT before pointerup.

fanout.degradation: Implementation parallelism is limited by shared high-conflict files WorkflowRoute.tsx and index.css; implementation waves are sequenced where write sets overlap.

decisions: Workspace Explorer file drags into the canvas create reference File nodes, not copied files.
External files/images dropped or pasted into the canvas are stored under Harness/user-files and represented as File nodes.
Pasted large text into the canvas creates a Markdown node.
For this slice, all node connections are effectively bidirectional by default, with permission/port metadata reserved for later refinement.
Markdown default output is controlled by an agent setting; if multiple connected Markdown nodes exist and no explicit target is selected, use the earliest-created Markdown node.
Agent settings should hide raw JSON for common permission and launch policy controls, while preserving an advanced area only for genuinely advanced fields.
Markdown and Diagram nodes should offer enlarged editing; Diagram should use the open-source Excalidraw package already installed in the UI workspace.
React error #185 is treated as a P0 update-loop regression and must be cleared by CDP/browser evidence before acceptance.
WebSocket is reserved for invalidation events in this slice, not file byte streaming.
Service Worker and WASM are out of default scope unless profiling proves they solve a specific bottleneck.
risks: Current graph state has backend, localStorage, and IndexedDB paths; keeping more than one source of truth can recreate disappearing edge bugs.
File previews for PDF/image/video/Excel can grow scope quickly; first slice should use browser-native viewers plus lightweight text/CSV support and avoid heavy parsers unless already available.
Changing node creation and settings UI touches a large WorkflowRoute component; implementation parallelism must respect write-set conflicts.
The worktree already contains partial prior edits and unrelated dirty files; Workers must not revert unrelated user changes.
React #185 may hide a state subscription loop that only appears in production/minified builds.
